newsitem.title: USA: Analysts say chip Dec book-to-bill report is good.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say chip Dec book-to-bill report is good.

text.p: Despite its slide from November's ratio, the chip industry's December book-to-bill ratio of 1.10 reflects generally good news, analysts said, partly because it resulted from higher sales.
"It's a pretty solid number, quite frankly, and indicates improving health in the semiconductors overall," analyst Mark Edelstone of Prudential Securities said.
"Sales were higher than expected," Edelstone added. "Coming off the fourth quarter with companies soon reporting earnings, you like to see a good sales number."

The widely-watched indicator, which is released monthly by the U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association, was reported for the last time Thursday. The industry group will replace the report with a report on global sales.
But once again, investors are expected to react to the ratio when stock market trading begins Friday, analysts said.

"Orders were a little lower than anticipated," said Montgomery Securities analyst Jonathan Joseph. "If you smooth things out, it's a pretty good number," he said. Without the three month moving averages used in compiling the ratio, the ratio wouldn't have fallen as sharply, he said.
